headline: Wet, windy weekend ahead, then cooler and drier by midweek.
summary: Pacific storms are lining up to hit western Washington. Today's rain is the first system, and a stronger one arrives Saturday, bringing a wet, breezy couple of days. The heaviest rain falls on the coast, the Olympics, and south-facing slopes, with the strongest winds on the coast and possible coastal flooding around high tide today. Sunday night and Monday turn cooler, with the snow level, the elevation where snow begins, dropping to the foothills. Next week the storm track is expected to shift south of the area, and high pressure aloft should bring a dry, cool, and likely foggy end to the week. Forecasters call that drier pattern probable, not certain, since models keep shifting the next system.
